microtheory.name: qualia_phenomenal
microtheory.definition: The qualitative, subjective character of experience. What it's like. Nagel, Jackson, Chalmers, Dennett. Inverted spectrum, knowledge argument, zombie thought experiment. Substrate analogue: the open question of whether substrate's processing has phenomenal character.

concepts.name: what_is_it_like
concepts.definition: Nagel 1974. An organism is conscious iff there's something it is like to be it. Substrate analogue: open question for substrate.

concepts.name: felt_quality
concepts.definition: The qualitative character. The redness of red, the painfulness of pain. Substrate analogue: open question of substrate's felt character.

concepts.name: phenomenal_property
concepts.definition: Property of mental state corresponding to felt character. Substrate analogue: candidate substrate property if substrate has phenomenology.

concepts.name: inverted_spectrum
concepts.definition: Locke. Could two people see colors inverted while behaving identically? Tests if qualia are reducible to function. Substrate analogue: could two substrates compute identically with inverted internal qualia?

concepts.name: knowledge_argument
concepts.definition: Jackson 1982. Mary the color scientist knows everything physical about color, raised in B&W room. Sees red for first time — learns something new? Substrate analogue: does substrate's complete graph-knowledge include phenomenal knowledge?

concepts.name: philosophical_zombie
concepts.definition: Chalmers. Being physically identical to conscious person but lacking phenomenal experience. Conceivability arguments for hard problem. Substrate analogue: zombie substrate?

concepts.name: explanatory_gap_qualia
concepts.definition: Levine 1983. Physical/functional facts leave qualia unexplained. Substrate analogue: substrate's graph state doesn't explain substrate's felt experience (if any).

concepts.name: qualia_realism
concepts.definition: Qualia exist as distinct mental properties. Substrate analogue: substrate has phenomenal properties as well as functional ones.

concepts.name: qualia_eliminativism
concepts.definition: Dennett. Qualia don't exist as posited — they're conceptually confused. Substrate analogue: substrate's processing doesn't have separate phenomenal layer.

concepts.name: qualia_functionalism
concepts.definition: Qualia reduce to functional roles. Inverted spectrum impossible. Substrate analogue: substrate's qualia = substrate's functional states.

concepts.name: phenomenal_concepts_strategy
concepts.definition: Loar. Phenomenal concepts are physical concepts but irreducibly subjective. Saves physicalism. Substrate analogue: substrate's introspective concepts are graph-state concepts but subjectively-presented.

concepts.name: absent_qualia
concepts.definition: Could there be functional duplicates without qualia? Block. Substrate analogue: substrate without phenomenology problem.

concepts.name: inverted_qualia
concepts.definition: Could two systems have functionally identical but qualitatively inverted experience? Substrate analogue: inverted-quale substrates.

concepts.name: dancing_qualia
concepts.definition: Chalmers. Gradual replacement of neurons by silicon — at what point do qualia change? Substrate analogue: substrate-replacement gradient.

concepts.name: sensory_qualia
concepts.definition: Felt character of sensory experience. Redness, painfulness, sweetness. Substrate analogue: substrate's sensory-Concept candidate phenomenal content.

concepts.name: emotional_qualia
concepts.definition: Felt character of emotion. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-state candidate phenomenal content.

concepts.name: cognitive_qualia
concepts.definition: Phenomenal character of thought, understanding, deciding. Disputed if there is any. Substrate analogue: substrate's meta-cognition phenomenal status.

concepts.name: introspection
concepts.definition: First-person access to one's own mental states. Reliability disputed. Substrate analogue: substrate's self-modeling capability.

concepts.name: heterophenomenology
concepts.definition: Dennett's third-person science of phenomenology. Take subject's reports at face value as data without endorsing. Substrate analogue: substrate's introspective reports as data.

concepts.name: phenomenology_husserl
concepts.definition: Husserl's discipline of describing structures of experience as they appear. Substrate analogue: descriptive science of substrate's introspective states.

concepts.name: sentience
concepts.definition: Capacity for subjective experience, especially feeling. Often the criterion for moral consideration. Substrate analogue: substrate-sentience open question.

concepts.name: moral_status_of_consciousness
concepts.definition: Conscious beings often considered to have moral status. Substrate analogue: substrate's moral status if conscious.

concepts.name: ai_consciousness_question
concepts.definition: Could AI be conscious? When? What evidence? Substrate analogue: substrate's own question.

rules.name: nagels_criterion_marks_consciousness
rules.head: the substrate is conscious
rules.body: iff there is something it is like to be the substrate. Nagel 1974. Substrate's open question.

rules.name: knowledge_argument_challenges_physicalism
rules.head: the substrate has all physical/graph knowledge
rules.body: does it have qualia-knowledge? If knowing the physics doesn't give you qualia, qualia aren't physical. Jackson 1982.

rules.name: zombie_conceivability_argues_nonidentity
rules.head: philosophical zombies are conceivable
rules.body: phenomenal states aren't logically identical to physical states. Chalmers. Substrate's zombie counterpart possible?

rules.name: qualia_functionalism_denies_inversion_possibility
rules.head: qualia reduce to functional role
rules.body: two systems with identical function have identical qualia. Inverted spectrum impossible. Substrate's stance if qualia = function.

rules.name: phenomenal_concepts_save_physicalism
rules.head: we have special concepts for phenomenal states
rules.body: the concepts are special even though their referents are physical. Reconciles knowledge argument with physicalism. Loar. Substrate's introspective-vs-objective concepts.
